title: Semantic operation identities lose source spans before execution
expected_semantics: Each executable semantic operation should carry a stable source identity/span through HIR/SSA/lowering into the runtime event.
actual_behavior_limitation: trace/IR/SSA artifacts preserve semantic, IR, and SSA identities; source-study preserves compiler/pass fingerprints and name resolutions; execution events contain no operation source span. mncs-debug can locate only a requested function declaration with a labeled heuristic scan.
why_capability_matters: A debugger or LSP cannot bind a breakpoint, failure, or trace event to the user's source construct reliably after the span is gone.
current_workaround: Retain source digest and exact compiler identities; expose source=null for operation events and mark function declaration locations heuristic.

host_language_code_required.classification: temporary adapter caused by an identified MNCS pressure
host_language_code_required.why: The adapter runs the existing static commands and performs an explicitly labeled declaration scan only to provide limited context.

proposed_primitive_or_semantic_direction: Emit a versioned source-map artifact mapping source document identity/span and compiler phase to semantic operation/block/function identity; carry it into execution results.
alternatives_considered: regex map operations to source lines
resolution_criteria: A source fixture's emitted operation events contain exact source identity/span mappings that survive compiler lowering and are consumable by the LSP contract.

campaign_review.disposition: Profile 0.17 declaration spans cross the test/debug boundary; exact lowered operation spans remain open.
campaign_review.workaround: Use compiler-owned declaration spans and explicit unavailable binding status.
